summary:
Düzce stands under the national framework of Turkey. The source inventory for this province records no Düzce-specific incident, enforcement practice or local instrument, so the assessment rests on the national regime a visitor to Düzce is subject to.

Consensual same-sex activity has been legal in Turkey since the 1858 Ottoman penal code, and legal gender change has been available since 1988. Turkish marriage law gives same-sex relationships no legal recognition and provides no civil unions, domestic partnerships or joint adoption. No comprehensive law bans discrimination on sexual orientation or gender identity, and LGBTQ people are barred from open military service.

In early 2026 Turkish media reported that the government was considering legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex'; that provision was not included in that year's judicial reform package. Amnesty International records that Pride events and LGBTQ gatherings were repeatedly disallowed in 2024 and 2025, with police detaining participants.
tangentialFactors: Düzce is an interior province with no documented LGBTQ-specific policing incident of its own in the inventory. The absence of a local record should not be read as a lower-risk finding: the national detention and ID-check patterns documented elsewhere in Turkey apply to interior provinces as well, and the inventory contains no evidence of differential local practice.
localsOnly: Residents of Düzce live under the same national legal position as visitors: legal gender change has been available since 1988, but there is no statutory discrimination protection on sexual orientation or gender identity, no recognition of same-sex relationships, and no route to joint adoption. Open military service is closed to LGBTQ people.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether the draft package reported in early 2026 has since been enacted is unresolved in the sources. No Düzce-specific enforcement data, detention records or local municipal instruments on LGBTQ matters were present in the inventory; the province-level picture is therefore an absence of signal rather than a positive finding of safety.
